sanskrit_verse:
नष्टस्यान्वेषणे कालं दद्यात् प्रतिभुवे धनी ।
देशाध्वरूपतः पक्षं मासं सार्धमथापि वा ॥
transliteration: naṣṭasyānveṣaṇe kālaṃ dadyāt pratibhuve dhanī / deśādhvarūpataḥ pakṣaṃ māsaṃ sārdham athāpi vā //
sph_interpretive_translation: The owner of wealth shall grant time for the search of the lost item according to the nature of the place, journey, and form; a fortnight, a month, or even more.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from ownership and responsibility
Causation is determined by contextual capacity
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with situational complexity
Restoration logic prioritizes completion over blame
Consciousness alignment requires honoring sequential manifestation
executable_legal_axioms: IF an item is lost THEN the owner must allocate search time proportional to context
CONTEXT includes: geographical scope, travel distance, and nature of the item
ALLOCATED TIME must not exceed one month unless justified by causal complexity
NO penalty accrues during lawful search period
RESTORATION occurs upon recovery OR conscious acknowledgment of non-recovery
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this axiom establishes that temporal allocation for restitution must reflect true causal conditions rather than punitive urgency. The court must recognize the primacy of completion over coercion, ensuring that executive enforcement aligns with dharmic capacity rather than judicial pressure.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality recognizes that time required for retrieval depends on deśa (place), adhvā (journey), and rūpataḥ (form/nature). This sequence ensures proportional responsibility without inflicting suffering. Anupūrvaśaḥ maintains that resolution unfolds naturally when consciousness is unobstructed by punitive interference.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Establish clear communication between claimant and custodian regarding search duration
Document all efforts made within allocated timeframe
Facilitate mutual agreement extension if causal complexity warrants
Upon expiration, both parties affirm either return or conscious release
Enforce no external compulsion—reality itself adjusts through alignment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: Time granted for recovery restores integrity, upholds ownership, and reflects pure consciousness in action. There is no punishment here—only alignment with what is.
